variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A monolith is one application that is built and deployed as one unit. A microservice is a smaller application with a clear business responsibility, its own deployable boundary, and an explicit contract with other services. A migration moves selected responsibilities out of a monolith gradually; it is not a rewrite and it is not a goal to maximize service count.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “What is a monolith-to-microservices migration?”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Name the constraint
pairs.detail: Capture the blocked release, overloaded capability, ownership conflict, or reliability target.
pairs.explanation: Capture the blocked release, overloaded capability, ownership conflict, or reliability target. A service boundary must solve one of these concrete problems.

pairs.label: Prove a boundary in-process
pairs.detail: Give a module one vocabulary, one write owner, and an interface that other modules use instead of reaching into its tables.
pairs.explanation: Give a module one vocabulary, one write owner, and an interface that other modules use instead of reaching into its tables.

pairs.label: Extract a narrow path
pairs.detail: Put a router in front of one capability, retain the previous path, and move traffic only after behavior and operations are observable.
pairs.explanation: Put a router in front of one capability, retain the previous path, and move traffic only after behavior and operations are observable.

pairs.label: Transfer ownership
pairs.detail: Move deployment, on-call, data ownership, service objectives, and recovery responsibility with the extracted capability.
pairs.explanation: Move deployment, on-call, data ownership, service objectives, and recovery responsibility with the extracted capability.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Use the full lesson’s worked examples and interactive labs to explore the trade-offs behind these questions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Name the constraint: Capture the blocked release, overloaded capability, ownership conflict, or reliability target. Prove a boundary in-process: Give a module one vocabulary, one write owner, and an interface that other modules use instead of reaching into its tables. Extract a narrow path: Put a router in front of one capability, retain the previous path, and move traffic only after behavior and operations are observable. Transfer ownership: Move deployment, on-call, data ownership, service objectives, and recovery responsibility with the extracted capability.

variants.prompt: Which condition most strongly supports extracting a capability from a modular monolith?
options: It has a stable business vocabulary, a clear owner, and an independently valuable scaling or release need
The team wants to increase its service count
Every database table can become an API
The capability has no fallback or operational owner
variants.explanation: A useful boundary solves a concrete organizational, scaling, release, or reliability constraint and has clear domain ownership.

variants.prompt: A checkout system receives 2,000 requests per second, and 30% call a new shipping service. With 40% headroom, what sustainable capacity should the new service plan for before retries?
options: 600 requests per second
800 requests per second
1,000 requests per second
2,000 requests per second
variants.explanation: Thirty percent of 2,000 is 600 requests per second. If that is 60% of planned sustainable capacity, capacity is 600 divided by 0.60, or 1,000 requests per second.

variants.prompt: Why is a checkout service writing directly to the inventory service's database a boundary failure?
options: It avoids all network latency
It leaves two components coupled to inventory schema and write rules
It guarantees distributed transactions
It makes inventory more independently owned
variants.explanation: A service boundary transfers authority as well as deployment. Direct database writes bypass the inventory owner's contract and preserve hidden coordination.
